pure-announcement.rationale: It markets the Fireworks platform heavily, but it is a benchmark-study writeup whose worker/advisor harness pattern and trajectory-filtering SFT recipe transfer beyond the product.

duplicate.rationale: Weak-to-strong generalization is the nearest neighbour but covers the training-supervision direction, not this inference-time pattern of an open worker invoking a frontier advisor as a tool.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The claims are anchored to Harvey's open-sourced 1,250-task LAB benchmark and named public models, so the runs are reproducible in principle despite being vendor-reported.

durability.rationale: The load-bearing content is model versions, pass rates and dollar costs (GLM 5.1 at 18/100 for $368 vs Opus at $954) that will be stale within months, even though the underlying harness pattern ages well.

actionability.rationale: A builder can act on two concrete recipes — let an open-source worker self-invoke a frontier advisor sparingly as a callable tool, and SFT on the completions that pass the benchmark rubric — both stated with enough mechanism to reproduce.

atomicity.rationale: It bundles two separable techniques the post itself treats as counterparts — inference-time harness engineering with a frontier advisor, and post-training via SFT/RFT on LAB trajectories — each of which could stand alone as a concept.
